title: Guidelines for Genetic Sample Collection of Small Mustelids
author: Andrin C. Dürst
materials: Use clean, sterilized tools (scissors, scalpel, forceps).
Consistently formatted to ensure interoperability across datasets.
Printed labels are preferred over handwritten tags.

steps.title: Obtain permits and ethical approvals
steps.instruction: Secure all required collection permits, CITES documentation, and ethical approvals for live‑animal handling or carcass recovery; verify that permits match the sample type (live, dead, export) and jurisdiction.

steps.title: Prepare equipment and safety measures
steps.instruction: Wear disposable gloves, use clean, sterilized tools (scissors, scalpel, forceps) for each animal or sample, and have water‑ and ethanol‑resistant labeling supplies ready.

steps.title: Verify species identity and record origin
steps.instruction: The designated coordinator must confirm taxonomic identity to species level; if uncertain, record the uncertainty (e.g., Mustela sp. or M. erminea ?) and attach supporting photos or field notes. Link each sample to metadata describing where, when, how, and by whom it was collected.

steps.title: Collect tissue samples
steps.instruction: Prioritise tissue from dead animals in this order: (1) heart muscle, (2) liver, (3) hind‑limb muscle, tongue, or back muscle. Dissect as soon as possible, cut pieces of at least 0.5–1 cm³, and keep each piece ≤ grain‑of‑rice size (≈20–30 mg) or larger if possible. Collect multiple small pieces rather than one large chunk and avoid placing excessive mass in a single container.

steps.title: Preserve tissue samples
steps.instruction: Choose one of the following preservation methods:

substeps.instruction: A) Ethanol + freezing (preferred): place tissue in 95–100 % ethanol (ratio ≥ 1:5 tissue:ethanol by volume) in tightly sealed screw‑cap microcentrifuge tubes, then freeze at ≤ ‑20 °C (‑80 °C ideal).
B) Freezing only: freeze immediately at ≤ ‑20 °C; for long‑term storage (months‑years) store at ‑80 °C; avoid repeated freeze‑thaw cycles.
C) Ethanol only: store in 95–100 % ethanol with the same 1:5 ratio; change ethanol after 24 h only for large tissue pieces; use sealed, clearly labelled containers.

steps.title: Collect hair with follicles
steps.instruction: Using clean forceps, remove hair from the tail base (do not collect whiskers from live animals). Aim for a tuft of ≈10 hairs that includes follicles; collect several small tufts rather than one large bundle to minimise skin trauma. Wear gloves and work on a clean surface to avoid contamination. Do not use cut or shed hairs lacking roots.

steps.title: Collect whole scat samples
steps.instruction: Gather the entire scat whenever possible; never pool scats from different individuals. Handle scats with clean forceps, tweezers, or gloves (avoid direct hand contact). Place each scat in a clean, labelled screw‑cap tube or zip‑lock bag and record its physical state (fresh, dry, old, desiccated, washed‑out, etc.).

steps.title: Preserve scat samples
steps.instruction: Select one preservation method based on field conditions:

substeps.instruction: A) Silica‑gel drying (preferred): place scat in an acid‑free breathable bag (paper or filter) or on sterile wadding, then into an airtight container with a minimum 5:1 weight ratio of silica gel to scat. Keep silica dry; replace if saturated (indicator colour). Store in a cool, dry, dark place away from UV, moisture and heat.
B) Freezing: put scat in a leak‑proof container and freeze at ≤ ‑20 °C (colder if possible). Use a cooling box in the field and avoid freeze‑thaw cycles.
C) Ethanol (95–100 %): submerge scat fully in ethanol in a leak‑proof tube; note this is not the first‑choice method because the faecal material disintegrates.

steps.title: Label samples with unique IDs
steps.instruction: Assign each sample a unique identifier using the format: [CountryCode]-[Year]-[InstitutionCode]-[TaxonCode]-[SampleType]-[SampleNumber][LetterSuffix] (e.g., SE-2025-NRMXX-MuEr-SCT-0034b). Write the ID with ethanol‑proof ink or pencil on a water‑ and ethanol‑resistant label, and place the label both inside and outside the container when possible. Ensure the label matches the ID recorded in the metadata file.

steps.title: Record and back up metadata
steps.instruction: Enter all sample information into a standardized Excel (or compatible) spreadsheet following the Darwin Core (DwC) schema, with optional GGBN extensions. Include fields for species, location, date, collector, permit numbers, physical state, preservation method, and unique ID. Back up the file locally and on institutional storage regularly.

steps.title: Store samples under appropriate conditions
steps.instruction: Keep samples in securely closed, robust containers that prevent cross‑contamination (especially for low‑DNA materials like hair and scat). Store tissue at the chosen temperature (‑20 °C or ‑80 °C), ethanol‑preserved samples at room temperature away from light, silica‑gel‑dried scats in a cool, dry place, and hair either frozen, ethanol‑preserved, or silica‑gel‑dried as described. Maintain a clean storage area and monitor for container integrity.

steps.title: Maintain custody and access agreements
steps.instruction: Retain samples at the collecting institution or individual; no central repository currently exists. Establish mutual agreements for future sharing, respecting national and institutional policies. The coordinator should verify identity and documentation for any third‑party‑provided samples.

steps.title: Optional supplementary sample types
steps.instruction: If resources allow, collect additional materials: oral/rectal/skin swabs (air‑dry and store dry in sterile tubes), blood (under veterinary oversight, store in ethanol or EDTA buffer and freeze). Detailed protocols for these are not included here.

steps.title: Photograph specimens and record measurements
steps.instruction: Take photographs of the whole animal, sampling site, and head with throat patch; label image files with the sample ID. Record measurements: head and neck circumference (cm), body and tail length (cm), hind foot length (cm), and weight (g).
